subject: Aurora - alignment on uptime targets, credits, and maintenance blackout windows
messages:
From: Aurora Procurement <procurement@aurora.ht>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Aurora - SLA redlines (MSA & Order Form)

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for the draft MSA and order form. Attached are Aurora's redlines focusing on uptime targets, service credits, response times, and maintenance windows. High-level asks:
- Move uptime to 99.99% for critical endpoints (production inference API)
- Remove the 30% annual cap on service credits
- 1-hour response for P1 incidents during business hours
- No scheduled maintenance during our month-end close windows (first 3 business days of each month)

Can we schedule a call this week to align? Prefer Wed or Thu morning PT.

Attachments:
- Aurora_MSA_redline_v1.pdf (pdf)
- OrderForm_SLA_Table.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Thanks,
Lina Park
Sr. Procurement Manager
Aurora HealthTech
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Aurora Procurement <procurement@aurora.ht>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-20T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Aurora - SLA redlines (MSA & Order Form)

Lina — thanks for sending these over. We've reviewed at a high level and there are a few items we need clarification on before a call.

Key notes:
1) Uptime: Aurora's ask for 99.99% across production inference endpoints is material. Can you confirm whether this is required for all endpoints or only a subset (e.g., model-hosting inference vs. batch embeddings)?
2) Credits cap: removing the annual cap exposes us to outsized risk. We typically propose an annual maximum credits cap (we propose 30% of fees in a 12-mo period) or a monthly sliding cap. Would Aurora consider a higher cap than 30% but not unlimited?
3) Response times: 1-hour P1 during business hours — is this local business hours or 24/7? Our standard P1 is 1 hour P1 for customers on enterprise support; need to confirm support tier for this deal.
4) Maintenance blackout: month-end blackout sounds reasonable but we need to define 'month-end close'; propose a fixed window (first 3 business days) for each region where Aurora runs close.

We'll prepare a clean counterproposal and list of acceptable endpoints. Can we do Wed 3/24 9:30am PT for an alignment call? Marissa and Karthik are looped for legal and infra inputs.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Head of Sales, Americas
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Aurora Procurement <procurement@aurora.ht>
Date: 2026-03-21T10:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Aurora - SLA redlines (MSA & Order Form) — legal input

Jonas / Karthik / Lina,

Quick legal POV on Aurora's redlines: thanks for the clear asks, Lina. Below are practical counters that limit Redwood's exposure while addressing Aurora's operational needs.

1) Uptime: 99.99% is aggressive for public inference endpoints. Proposal: 99.95% for the production inference API (the endpoint that serves live, low-latency inference) and 99.9% for non-critical embedding/batch endpoints. This gives Aurora higher availability where it matters while keeping realistic expectations for multi-region failover windows.

2) Service credits cap: we cannot accept an open-ended removal. Counterproposal: increase the cap to 40% of fees in a rolling 12-month window (up from our standard 30%). Alternatively, accept unlimited credits but tier them (e.g., escalating credits for sustained outages) with an overall annual cap tied to subscription value.

3) Response times: clarify support commitment — if Aurora requires 1-hour P1 24/7, that changes resourcing. If 1-hour P1 is limited to Aurora's business hours (define timezone), we can accept at no additional cost. For 24/7 1-hour P1 we will need an enterprise support add-on or a higher price.

4) Maintenance blackout: define 'month-end close' explicitly. We can agree to a blackout for the first 3 business days of each month for production endpoints with a caveat: scheduled maintenance requested >30 days out is excluded, and emergency security patches retain a narrow carveout (we propose a 12-hour emergency maintenance window with immediate notification).

Next steps: I will prepare a tracked counter MSA and order form with inline language and a short commentary explaining the commercial impact of each change. Also recommend we include Aurora's SOC2 Type II report and an evidence pack (audit logs, retention policy) into the procurement packet.

If we can't land the credit cap via wording, commercial should prepare a dollars-for-credits trade (e.g., 12% price uplift for removing the cap).

-Marissa
Marissa Cole
General Counsel, Commercial
Redwood Inference

From: Aurora Procurement <procurement@aurora.ht>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-21T15:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Aurora - SLA redlines (MSA & Order Form)

Jonas / Marissa / Karthik,

Thanks for the quick replies and the proposed counters. A few clarifications and pushes from Aurora's side:

• Uptime: We need 99.99% for any endpoint that serves live patient-facing inference (low-latency API). Batch/analytics endpoints are fine at 99.9%. The clinical risk profile for the product requires the tighter SLA.
• Credits cap: removing the cap was intentional — Aurora cannot accept a hard ceiling that could allow prolonged degraded service without meaningful remediation. If Redwood requires a cap, Aurora is open to a higher cap than 40% but would prefer a combined remedy (credits + scheduled remediation SLA) rather than a hard cap alone.
• Response times: 1-hour P1 must be 24/7. Our product support runs round-the-clock and patient impact can occur any time.
• Maintenance blackout: Thanks for the definition suggestions. The first 3 business days of each month are mandatory blackout windows for production in our primary region (US-West). We accept a narrow emergency patch carveout but only with immediate rollback guarantees and post-action incident report.

We can do a short call tomorrow (Tue) 3/22 at 10:00am PT to discuss tradeoffs and finalize the counter. If we can't settle on credits wording, we'll expect commercial pricing adjustments.

Best,
Lina Park
Sr. Procurement Manager
Aurora HealthTech

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-22T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: Aurora negotiation plan and next steps

Marissa / Karthik — after Lina's notes, here's how I'd like to proceed ahead of tomorrow's call with Aurora.

Summary of points to take to call:
- Uptime: push for the 99.95% / 99.9% split as Marissa proposed, but draft a narrow carveout for clinically-critical production endpoints where Aurora can pay an uplift for 99.99% and 24/7 1-hour P1. That gives us a commercial lever.
- Credits: offer the 40% rolling 12-mo cap as legal suggested but pair it with an SLA remediation schedule (e.g., automatic incident postmortem, engineering priority queue SLA, and a one-time remediation credit beyond the cap if outage exceeds X hours). Prepare a pricing uplift option if Aurora insists on removing the cap.
- Response times: confirm whether Aurora will purchase 24/7 enterprise support. If yes, we accept 1-hour P1 24/7 as a defined add-on.
- Maintenance blackout: accept first 3 business-day blackout for US-West for production endpoints, with a strict emergency patch process (12-hour emergency window + rollback guarantee + incident report).

Action items before call (I can cover scheduling):
1) Marissa: prepare tracked MSA/order form with the 40% cap + remediation schedule language and an optional addendum for the 99.99%/24x7 support priced uplift.
2) Karthik: prepare a short engineering note on what achieving 99.99% for selected endpoints entails (multi-region standby, warm pools, failover RTO estimates) and expected monthly cost delta. Attach as a one-page appendix.
3) Commercial (me): draft two pricing options (base + 40% cap, base+uplift for unlimited credits) and the DocuSign skeleton.

Call is scheduled: 2026-03-23T10:00:00-07:00 (Aurora requested 3/22 but we pushed to 3/23 to align internal). Please review and add any items you want on the agenda.
